title: Warehouse rover in Isaac Sim
details: Built warehouse_rover.py in NVIDIA Isaac Sim 5.1: a Nova Carter rover in the Simple Warehouse scene drives to 4 coloured waste objects using an Artificial Potential Field (APF) planner written in pure Python, then plays a 3-second pickup animation. A second script builds procedural grassy uneven terrain.

title: Project proposal written
details: Wrote the BE project proposal: an autonomous waste-collection mobile manipulator, simulation first, with a two-layer simulation idea (a detailed world, but a robot model that behaves like the real hardware).

title: Funding request sent
details: Applied to the college Student Project Financial Assistance Scheme for 2026-27 to fund the rover hardware.

title: Pi set up with ROS 2 Jazzy
details: Flashed Ubuntu Server 24.04 on the Raspberry Pi 5 (headless, no screen), installed ROS 2 Jazzy and checked it with the talker and listener demo. Ordered the RPLiDAR A1M8. The first 5 V BO motors burned out and were replaced.

title: Hardware PWM on the Pi 5
details: PWM writes on the Pi 5 failed with 'Invalid argument'. Cause: wrong PWM channel numbers and a missing setting in the device tree overlay. Fixed with the right channels (GPIO18 and GPIO19) and dtoverlay=pwm-2chan,clock=50000000 in config.txt.

title: Component layout planned
details: Planned where each board sits. LiDAR raised above everything and close to the centre. Pi and motor driver kept off the bare metal plate (insulated) to avoid short circuits. Battery low and between the axles.
captions: The bare chassis. Masking tape on the metal plate stops the boards from shorting against it.

title: First motor control code
details: Wrote the TB6612FNG motor driver code, a bench test (direction check and deadband sweep) and keyboard driving over SSH with an auto-stop if commands stop arriving.
captions: The Pi 5 and our soldered motor driver board, joined by the GPIO ribbon cable.

title: Motors spin under software control
details: First time the wheels moved from code. The left motor ran backwards because it is mounted as a mirror image, fixed in software with LEFT_INVERTED = True. Also reflashed the SD card after a login problem caused by the keyboard layout.
captions: Top view: Pi 5, the TB6612FNG on our perfboard, the GPIO extension board and the battery lead.

title: LiDAR cable rebuilt
details: The cable between the RPLiDAR A1M8 and its USB adapter board was lost, so we made our own. A third-party wiring guide was right where the official pin labels did not match the adapter for 3 pins, so every pin was checked with a multimeter continuity test before soldering.

title: Gazebo simulation of the rover
details: Simulated the rover in Gazebo Harmonic with ROS 2 Jazzy on WSL2 (Ubuntu 24.04). One launch file starts Gazebo, laser odometry, SLAM Toolbox, Nav2 and RViz. Simulation runs on its own ROS channel so it can never send commands to the real rover.

title: First map and goals on the real rover
details: With 2 driven wheels and a ball caster, the real rover mapped a college corridor with SLAM, then reached goal points on its own with Nav2 on the saved map. Laser odometry only, no wheel encoders. The default speed was too slow.

title: Moved to a 4-wheel skid-steer rover
details: Removed the caster and fitted 4 x 12 V BO motors (first 500 RPM, exchanged for 200 RPM), skid steer, all on one TB6612FNG (left pair on channel A, right pair on channel B). The driver stays cool. Size 28 x 24.5 cm, wheelbase 18 cm, track 22 cm. LiDAR faces backwards, 8.5 cm in front of centre, laser height 21.5 cm.
captions: The 4-wheel rover: Pi 5 in its case, the 5 V converter, the motor driver and the IMU, with the LiDAR ready to mount on top.

title: IMU added for sensor fusion
details: Our guide asked for multi-sensor fusion (LiDAR plus another sensor), so we added an MPU6050 IMU on I2C. It works when the rover is still, but motor noise makes it freeze (see 22 below).

title: Gazebo twin of the 4-wheel rover
details: Updated the simulation to the 4-wheel rover using the same robot model file as the real rover, with a simulated LiDAR at about 7 scans per second like the A1M8.

phase: Making it work on the real rover
title: Skid-steer turns stalled
details: On-spot turns need about 32-35% power just to start, so slow turns stalled. Fix in the motor node: a short kick at 42% power, then at least 38% sustain power, with a re-kick every 1.5 s and gentle slew ramps.

phase: Making it work on the real rover
title: Map and rover missing in RViz
details: RViz showed LiDAR scans but no map and no rover model. Cause: the FASTDDS_BUILTIN_TRANSPORTS=UDPv4 setting forced big messages through the WSL network, where they failed. Removing that line fixed it, and Nav2 reached goals.

phase: Making it work on the real rover
title: LiDAR drops during turns
details: LiDAR USB disconnected during on-spot turns. The kernel log said 'disabled by hub (EMI?)'. Cause: electrical noise from the 4 motors, which pull a lot of current while skid-steer turning. Scans stopped, so odometry and SLAM froze and Nav2 aborted goals. Added a LiDAR guard script that restarts the LiDAR automatically.

phase: Making it work on the real rover
title: Map drawn twice (star pattern)
details: After a LiDAR drop in the middle of a turn, SLAM matched scans at the wrong angle and drew walls twice. With no wheel encoders or IMU, SLAM depends only on scan matching. Fix: restart the map and drive gently.

phase: Making it work on the real rover
title: Noise capacitors fitted
details: Soldered capacitors at the noise sources: a 0.1 uF ceramic (104) across each of the 4 motors, 470 uF + 0.1 uF across the TB6612 motor supply (VM and GND), and 1000 uF + 0.1 uF across the converter's 5 V output to the Pi. After this, the LiDAR dropped much less often during turns.

phase: Making it work on the real rover
title: Curves too weak
details: While driving, Nav2 asked for strong curves but the two sides differed by only 8% power, so the rover drove almost straight and drifted off the path. Raised the curve gain from 2.0 to 6.0, so the sides now differ by about 25%.

phase: Making it work on the real rover
title: Faster and cleaner navigation
details: The rover never went above 0.20 m/s. Raised Nav2's top speed to 0.40 m/s for straight driving. Used the rover's real rectangle shape (30 x 26 cm) instead of a 40 cm circle, marked obstacles only up to 2.5 m away, and made the safety zone around obstacles thinner (0.30 m).

phase: Making it work on the real rover
title: IMU paused
details: Even with the capacitors, the IMU still fails 2-19% of readings while the motors run and can freeze completely after they stop. Before the capacitors it froze every time. Navigation does not need it, so it is switched off. Next ideas: capacitors at the IMU itself, a power reset from a GPIO pin, or reading it on an ESP32.

phase: Making it work on the real rover
title: Navigation moved onto the Pi
details: Running SLAM and Nav2 on the laptop over WiFi made navigation freeze. Moved SLAM and Nav2 onto the Pi 5. The laptop now only shows RViz.

phase: Making it work on the real rover
title: WiFi lag fixed
details: WiFi lag was about 1.2 s with 90% packet loss. Cause: WiFi power saving on the Pi. It is now switched off at every boot. After the fix: 171 of 171 pings arrived while driving, about 11 ms on average.

phase: Making it work on the real rover
title: Odometry ran backwards
details: On the Pi, the laser odometry got its first scan before the robot model was loaded, so it assumed the LiDAR faced forward. In RViz the rover moved backwards while the real rover drove forward. Fix: a small scan gate that holds scans until the LiDAR position is known, plus 3 seconds.

title: First full test run
details: In one 10-minute run before the final fixes, 16 of 20 goals were reached (27 were sent, but 7 were sent while the LiDAR was disconnected, so they could not start and are not counted). The 4 misses: 3 goals stopped because the LiDAR dropped out mid-trip from motor noise (the rover stopped itself, as designed), and 1 got stuck in a tight turn. 34+ m of autonomous travel, longest trip 5.4 m. The Pi 5 stayed at 48-52 C and never throttled.

title: LiDAR guard v3 and cable reconnected
details: The guard now resets the LiDAR's USB straight away when scans stop, and asks for a replug only if the USB does not come back. Reconnected our custom-made LiDAR cable, after which the LiDAR stopped dropping out.

title: Final run: 20 of 20
details: With all the fixes in place (noise capacitors, our own LiDAR cable, guard v3, stronger curves, the scan gate and the faster Nav2 settings), the final run reached all 20 of 20 goals, with no LiDAR drops.

title: Open Day presentation
details: Presented 'Autonomous Mobile Rover with Real-Time Mapping and Navigation' (team 6): manual control, real-time mapping and autonomous navigation on live and saved maps, in Gazebo and on the real rover. Did not win, but it went well.

title: Rover Knowledge Assistant
details: Built this website and a RAG question-answering assistant over our build notes, our workflow and the part datasheets, at the GAT Hack Hour.
